earth.summary: Earth stays up for the whole 29.5-day window

data_sources.ephemeris_source: NAIF SPICE kernels: naif0012.tls, de440s.bsp, moon_pa_de440_200625.bpc, moon_de440_250416.tf

limitations: Sun/Earth positions from the ephemeris backend (analytic Meeus model or SPICE DE440)
sunlit / visible = disk centre above the horizon; disk_visible_fraction gives partial disks
horizon from the DEM (360 azimuth bins, rays to 100 km) only where a DEM covers the site
events shorter than one sampling interval can be missed
power factors are geometry only: no panel efficiency, temperature or dust

Geometric line of sight to the Earth's centre only. Actual radio communication also depends on antenna pointing and gain, link budget, ground-station coverage on Earth, relay satellites and the lander's own terrain mask; it is not modelled here.

reasons: Longest night is 258 h, above the 100 h hard limit.
verdict.summary: The night is too long for a solar lander with about four days of battery under our assumptions.

verdict_explanation: Not viable: at least one condition is unfavorable under our simplified criteria. The night is too long for a solar lander with about four days of battery under our assumptions. Why: Longest night is 258 h, above the 100 h hard limit. This is an indicative assessment under our simplified assumptions, not a NASA certification.
